summary: Eritrea's embassy in Washington says a visa is required for non-Eritreans and for Eritreans without a national ID; Eritrea's Ministry of Information says Eritrea and Kenya agreed to abolish visa requirements for citizens travelling between the two countries from 9 February 2023. The UK, Canadian, Australian and Serbian governments say their citizens need one to enter. The Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says that upon receipt of the visa application and fees, issuance takes ten working days, and that there is no assurance that a visa will be issued. The UK government says foreign nationals must apply in advance for a permit to travel outside Asmara's surrounding province, Zoba Maekel.

tips.text: The UK government says foreign nationals must apply in advance for a permit to travel outside Asmara's surrounding province, Zoba Maekel, as well as to certain sites within the capital like the 'tank graveyard'. Tourists apply to the Ministry of Tourism; applications may take several days and are not always successful, and officials check permits at checkpoints outside Asmara.
The UK government advises against all travel to within 25 km of all of Eritrea's land borders; the Australian government says landmines are found within 25 km of Eritrea's border with Ethiopia.

The Government of Canada says credit cards are not accepted as a method of payment for everyday transactions and that foreign currency must be exchanged at a branch of Himbol, at main banks or in major hotels in Asmara; the UK government says foreign cash or travellers cheques worth 10,000 US dollars or more must be declared and that when you leave you must be able to show how any foreign currency you spent was exchanged or spent.

The UK government says internet access is highly restricted in Eritrea, mainly limited to hotels and a small number of internet cafes, that there is no 3G, that international SIM cards do not work, and that you need a residence permit to buy a local SIM card.

The UK government says photographing government buildings and military installations is illegal, and to always ask if you want to take a photo in any area where security personnel are present. The Government of Canada says photographing sensitive installations is prohibited, including airports, ports, military sites, government buildings and uniformed service members.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Eritrea?
faq.answer: Eritrea's embassy in Washington says a visa is required for non-Eritreans and for Eritreans without a national ID. Eritrea's Ministry of Information says Eritrea and Kenya agreed to abolish visa requirements for citizens travelling between the two countries from 9 February 2023. The UK, Canadian, Australian and Serbian governments say their citizens need one to enter. The Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says that upon receipt of the visa application and fees, issuance takes ten working days, and that there is no assurance that a visa will be issued.

faq.question: How long does an Eritrean visa take?
faq.answer: The Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says that upon receipt of the visa application and fees, issuance takes ten working days, and that a visa is valid for three months from the date of issue unless stated otherwise. It says there is no assurance that a visa will be issued.

faq.question: Can I travel outside Asmara in Eritrea?
faq.answer: Only with a travel permit. The UK government says foreign nationals must apply in advance for a permit to travel outside Asmara's surrounding province, Zoba Maekel, and to certain sites within the capital. Tourists apply to the Ministry of Tourism; applications may take several days and are not always successful, and officials check permits at checkpoints outside Asmara.

faq.question: Can I use cards or ATMs in Eritrea?
faq.answer: Not for everyday transactions: the Government of Canada says Eritrea has a cash-based economy, credit cards are not accepted as a method of payment for everyday transactions, and foreign currency must be exchanged at a branch of Himbol, at main banks or in major hotels in Asmara. The UK government says to declare foreign cash or travellers cheques worth 10,000 US dollars or more and keep the certificate you get to show when you leave, and that you must be able to show that any foreign currency you have spent was exchanged at Himbol or spent at an official hotel.

faq.question: Is Eritrea safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK government says that though Asmara is a relatively safe city, there is a risk of street crime, especially at night. It advises against all travel to within 25 km of all of Eritrea's land borders, says foreign nationals must apply in advance for a permit to travel outside Asmara's surrounding province and that international SIM cards do not work, and says British Embassy staff cannot always provide consular assistance in person outside Asmara.
